title: operator-preflight-checklist-major-rollouts-2026
author: Hannah Li
body:
Overview
--------
This document is a prescriptive operator preflight checklist for major platform rollouts (service version upgrades, model swaps, capacity migration, or cross-region launches). It consolidates the technical checks, telemetry verification, stakeholder coordination, and rollback criteria that platform operators must validate before promoting a change from canary to 100% production. Use this checklist as the canonical gate for ‘major’ changes that meet any of the following: impact more than 10% of traffic, alter model or runtime behavior, modify tenant isolation boundaries, or touch capacity/billing critical paths.

Scope and intent
----------------
- Scope: Redwood Inference platform services (runtime components, routing layer, tenant slicing, KV/prefix cache, autoscaling, and observability pipelines).
- Intent: Reduce blast radius for major changes using repeatable, measurable preflight validation.
- Not a replacement for per-service ADRs or release notes; link those artifacts in Related Pages.

Ownership and roles
-------------------
- Release Lead: coordinates the rollout, holds the final gate decision. (Typical: platform-release@redwood)
- Oncall/Operator: executes preflight checks, performs live telemetry verification.
- Service Owner: confirms functional correctness and approves behaviour and quality metrics.
- SRE/Observability: validates dashboards, alerting, and retention.
- Product/PM: confirms business acceptance criteria (if behaviour changes).

Quick acceptance criteria (pass/fail)
-----------------------------------
- Critical SLOs must be within degradation budget:
  - 99th perc latency for foreground requests not increased by more than 15% vs baseline for canary traffic.
  - Error rate increase must be < 0.05 percentage points in canary window.
- Token cost/unit request uplift must be within expected range per the preflight cost model.
- No new P0 errors or exceptions observed for 30 minutes under canary load.

Preflight checklist (operator-run)
---------------------------------
A. Administrative gates
1. Release ticket created with links to builds, images, and changelogs.
2. Rollout plan and timeline published in the release ticket (incl. rollback windows).
3. Primary and backup approvers assigned with contact info (pager and slack).

B. Build and artifact validation
1. Verify artifacts: container image digest, model bundle hash, and config commit sha match release ticket.
   - Example: docker image sha256:abc123... and model bundle md5: f1e2d3...
2. Confirm image provenance: signed by CI (cosign) and from the release registry.
3. Run lightweight smoke test command in staging: 
   - curl -sS -X POST https://staging-api.redwood.internal/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"smoke test"}' | jq .status

C. Capacity and scaling checks
1. Confirm capacity headroom across regions and GPU pools: free capacity >= planned burst + 20%.
2. Verify autoscaler params for this deployment: min_replicas, target_cpu, target_queue_latency.
   - Example YAML snippet for autoscaler: 
     minReplicas: 4
     maxReplicas: 40
     targetAvgQueueMs: 20
3. Run a short predictive-scale test against canary pool (non-customer tenants) and validate no eviction cascades.

D. Observability and telemetry
1. Dashboards: ensure the release dashboard is populated (latency, p95/p99, error-rate, token-cost-per-request).
   - Recommended dashboard panels: request qps, foreground p50/p95/p99 latency, KV cache hit ratio, GPU utilization, model-latency-by-sequence-length.
2. Confirm APM traces show correct service spans for the new version.
3. Clone synthetic traffic job for canary: run synthetic generator for 15m and verify no new high severity traces.
4. Validate Prometheus alert rules are active and routed. Sample PromQL checks to run: 
   - rate(http_requests_total{job="runtime", version="canary"}[5m])
   - increase(runtime_errors_total{job="runtime", version="canary"}[10m]) > 0

E. Cost and billing sanity
1. Run cost-projection script against canary sample to ensure estimated cost delta < threshold.
   - ./tools/cost-forecast --from canary-metrics --horizon 24h --threshold 12%
2. Tagging and metering verified: new instances and requests show expected token and tenant tags for attribution.

F. Safety nets and fallbacks configured
1. Model/service variant fallback configured with traffic steering rules in routing layer (route to previous-version or cheaper-quantized-variant).
2. Circuit breaker/timeout lower bounds set and tested.
   - Example default: 30s hard timeout; 10s soft timeout for foreground interactive requests.
3. Rate-limiting quotas bounded per-priority class with soft and hard thresholds, and throttling behavior documented.

G. Canary plan and traffic ramping
1. Canary traffic slice defined (e.g., 1% traffic for 20 minutes, then 5% for 30 minutes, etc.).
2. Automated ramping job exists and is configured to stop on any fail condition.
3. Health-check criteria for each step: latency, errors, cost, and per-tenant quality signals.

H. Rollback and rollback criteria
1. Explicit rollback playbook included in release ticket, with commands and owners.
2. Rollback criteria (examples):
   - p99 latency increases by > 25% for 5 continuous minutes.
   - error-rate increase > 0.1 percentage points sustained for 10 minutes.
   - SLO burn rate > 10x baseline for 15 minutes.
3. Automated rollback endpoint tested in staging: 
   - POST /api/admin/rollout/rollback -d '{"target":"previous"}'

I. Communication and coordination
1. Slack channel created (#release-<id>) and attendees from all owners present for the move.
2. Customer success and account owners notified for any customers in affected regions or on dedicated capacity.
3. Status page template prepared for any customer-visible incidents.

J. Post-deploy verification (first 2 hours)
1. 0% P0 incidents.
2. SLI checks every 5 minutes for the first hour, then every 15 minutes in hour 2.
3. Sampling-based quality checks for generation output (automated eval set against prompt-sets).

Operational snippets and commands
-------------------------------
- Query canary pods: kubectl -n runtime get pods -l app=runtime,version=canary - Describe autoscaler: kubectl -n infra get hpa runtime-canary -o yaml - Synthetic load run: k8s-job run synthetic-canary --image=redwood/tools:canary -- args='--profile=canary-small --duration=900'

Prometheus / Alert quick checks (examples)
---------------------------------------
- Canary error rate (5m):
  expr: increase(runtime_errors_total{env="prod", deployment="canary"}[5m]) / increase(http_requests_total{env="prod", deployment="canary"}[5m])
- Latency shift analyzer (p99 delta):
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{deployment="canary"}[5m])) by (le, job)) - histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{deployment="baseline"}[5m])) by (le, job))

Ownership and escalation matrix
------------------------------
- Release Lead: @hannah.li (primary)
- SRE oncall: see oncall rota (primary)
- Model owner: provided on release ticket
- Escalation: Pager duty runbook to reach Eng VP if rollback decision required in < 15 minutes.

Postmortem and retrospective expectations
---------------------------------------
- If rollback occurs or any P1/P0 incident happens, a postmortem must be filed within 72 hours and labelled with the release ticket.
- For non-trivial degradations (SLO burn > threshold) a 1-week mini-retrospective is required to tune canary gating and automation.

Templates and artifacts to attach (minimal)
-----------------------------------------
1. Release ticket link and CI artifact checksums.
2. Canary dashboard snapshot (PNG) and a short summary line of canary health.
3. Synthetic test output (stdout logs) and sampled traces ids.

Appendix A: Example canary ramp plan (time-based)
------------------------------------------------
- t=0: 1% traffic for 20 minutes (automated gate checks every 5m)
- t=20m: 5% traffic for 30 minutes
- t=50m: 20% traffic for 30 minutes
- t=80m: 50% traffic for 20 minutes
- t=100m: 100% traffic (final gate requires explicit Release Lead approval)

Appendix B: Quick rollback commands
-----------------------------------
- Force rollback via routing API: curl -X POST https://operator-api.internal/v1/route/override -d '{"service":"runtime", "target_version":"previous"}'
- Scale down canary pods: kubectl -n runtime scale deployment runtime-canary --replicas=0

Appendix C: Example acceptance table (to paste into release ticket)
------------------------------------------------------------------
- [ ] Build artifacts verified
- [ ] Canary dashboard created
- [ ] Synthetic test green
- [ ] Capacity verified (>= planned+20%)
- [ ] Fallback route configured and smoke-tested
- [ ] Rollback playbook present and executable

Notes and rationales
--------------------
- The 20% headroom requirement is conservative for multi-tenant GPU pools to absorb transient evictions and balancing.
- Short synthetic tests reduce noisy investigations; longer soak windows are used for performance-sensitive path changes.

Related pages and further reading
--------------------------------
- Canary orchestration DSL and safe rollback playbook (link in Related Pages).
- SLO rollbacks and degradation lab notebook for examples of threshold tuning.
